newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania sees economy contracting three pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Romania sees economy contracting three pct in 1997.

text.p: The Romanian economy is expected to contract three percent in 1997, Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara said on Thursday in presenting the budget to parliament.
"In working out this budget, we envisaged negative growth of three percent," Ciumara told a joint session of parliament.
"We expect that over the whole year industrial output will fall. But we hope that starting in June, July and August economic recovery will start and inflation will slow."
Ciumara said the government was standing by a forecast of 90 percent inflation for the year.
Figures released this week put inflation at 30.7 percent for March alone, against original forecasts of 10-12 percent, and brought the figure for the first three months to 76.5 percent.

The budget was being presented during a routine mission to Romania by an International Monetary Fund delegation, ahead of a decision later this month by the IMF board on whether to resume credits suspended last year to the Balkan country.
The head of the IMF delegation said parliamentary approval of the budget was vital for the government's reform programme.
Inflation last year stood at 56.9 percent.
Ciumara gave no specific figures for the proposed budget deficit but said it would be "bearable so that Romania can still be governed next year".
Previous government forecasts have put this year's deficit at 4.5 percent of economic output against last year's 5.7 percent - nearly three times higher than targets.
The IMf suspended credits to Romania last year after criticising the leftist government for overshooting spending targets and hobbling foreign exchange markets.
Ciumara said the new centrist administration, elected last November, could not immediately deliver on election promises to raise Romania's living standards.

"It is true that we promised Romanians a better life during the election campaign, but this cannot be done from the first days," he said. "We hope that with the nation's efforts 1997 will be the last tough year Romanians will have to bear."
